rows.title: Amazon.com Associates Central
rows.observed: Updated: April 14, 2026. Commission Income Statement item 1 (a)-(c) states the Session windows reported in the ledger record: 24 hours from the click, or an order completed within 89 days, and shipment/payment within 180 days. IP License 2(h) states that Product Advertising Content consisting of an image must not be stored or cached, though a link to an image may be stored for up to 24 hours; text content may be cached up to 24 hours if refreshed. IP License 2(k) prescribes the 'CERTAIN CONTENT THAT APPEARS...' notice beside Product Advertising Content consisting of text, which the site already prints. IP License 4 (Agent Terms) requires any Agent accessing Program Content to identify itself in its HTTP user-agent string as 'Agent/[agent name]' and forbids concealing that access is from an Agent or completing CAPTCHAs.
rows.matches_stored_record: Yes for the 'Updated' date (2026-04-14). The image rule, the text-content cache window and the Agent Terms are new readings for this repository's record and are the basis of F-68 and Q-56.
rows.note: No product value is taken from this page.

rows.title: Disclosures 101 for Social Media Influencers | Federal Trade Commission
rows.observed: Page dated November 2019. 'Make sure people will see and understand the disclosure'; 'Place it so it's hard to miss'; disclosures are likely to be missed if they appear only on an ABOUT ME or profile page, 'at the end of posts or videos, or anywhere that requires a person to click MORE'; 'You can't talk about your experience with a product you haven't tried.'
rows.matches_stored_record: Consistent with the site's standing disclosure rule (above the fold and in the footer). The 'click MORE' sentence is the official basis for keeping the disclosure above the fold on every page, including the long register pages.
rows.note: No product value is taken from this page.

rows.title: Creating Helpful, Reliable, People-First Content | Google Search Central
rows.observed: The page's quality questions include whether content provides 'original information, reporting, research, or analysis' and 'insightful analysis or interesting information that is beyond the obvious', and whether a page's main heading or title 'provides a descriptive, helpful summary of the content'. The page also says rankings are not a claim a site may make about itself.
rows.matches_stored_record: Consistent. This is the standard cited for S-47 through S-50 (the editorially distinctive content path) and for Q-53.
rows.note: Read for the editorial standard only; no ranking, traffic or demand figure is derived or reproduced.
